name: Integer Programming
description: Modelling with binary and integer variables, formulations and relaxations, alternative formulations and tightening, geometry of the integer lattice, connections with number theory and linear programming, convex hull, mixed-integer rounding, totally unimodular matrices, fundamental theorem of integer programming, computational complexity, branch-and-bound algorithm, valid inequalities, separation and optimization, cutting planes and branch-and-cut algorithm, cover inequalities and separation, duality in integer programming, submodularity, decomposition techniques - column generation and Bender's decomposition, practical considerations in integer programming - presolving, infeasibility detection, primal heuristics, warm-starting, etc., advanced topics in integer programming - mixed integer linear and convex representability, symmetry, interplay with AI/ML and quantum computing.
